title: TopNav
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigationsuite.NavigationSuiteScaffold, which shows androidx.compose.material3.NavigationBar or NavigationRail for the window size
summary: A TopNav is a single row of top-level destinations in a header: the brand mark at the start, the links (the current one in the subtle accent pill, a count badge), a More menu for the links that do not fit and a Share button at the end. Monarch composes it from its own parts, as the web TopNav does.
whenToUse: For three to five top-level destinations that the person switches between often. Use NavigationSuiteScaffold so the same list becomes a bar or a rail as the window changes.
whenNotToUse: For more destinations, or destinations in sections, use a navigation drawer (see sidebar-nav). For views of the same content use tabs (see tabs).
api: @Composable fun NavigationSuiteScaffold(navigationSuiteItems: NavigationSuiteScope.() -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layoutType: NavigationSuiteType = NavigationSuiteScaffoldDefaults.calculateFromAdaptiveInfo(currentWindowAdaptiveInfo()), navigationSuiteColors: NavigationSuiteColors = NavigationSuiteDefaults.colors(), containerColor: Color = NavigationSuiteScaffoldDefaults.containerColor, contentColor: Color = NavigationSuiteScaffoldDefaults.contentColor, content: @Composable () -> Unit)

fun NavigationSuiteScope.item(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, icon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, label: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, alwaysShowLabel: Boolean = true, badge: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, colors: NavigationSuiteItemColors? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

states.name: compact width
states.description: A NavigationBar at the bottom with an icon and a label per destination.

states.name: medium and expanded width
states.description: A NavigationRail at the start edge.

states.name: selected
states.description: The destination's icon sits in a pill of the subtle accent role and its label is the default text role.

states.name: with a count
states.description: A Badge or MonarchBadge in the item's badge slot.

appearance: The bar and the rail use the raised background role (Material surfaceContainer); the selected item's indicator is the subtle accent role (secondaryContainer) with the strong accent role for its icon, and other items use the muted text role. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web TopNav is a row of links in a page header that moves the links that do not fit into a More menu, with start and end slots. Android shows the same row: the start slot is the app mark, the end slot a secondary small Share button, the overflow is a MonarchMenu opened from More. It is a recipe built from MonarchButton, MonarchBadge and MonarchMenu, not a bottom bar. Use NavigationSuiteScaffold (see app-shell) only when the product wants a bottom bar on a phone. iOS uses the same top row.
accessibility: System behavior: each item has the tab role and the selected state, and is at least 48dp; TalkBack reads its label.
Keep labels visible (alwaysShowLabel = true); give an icon a null description when the label is shown.
The selected item has an indicator pill, not color alone.
The rail is at the start edge and mirrors in right to left.
edgeCases: Labels longer than one word are cut in a bar at the largest font size; keep them short.
The scaffold reads the window size class; in a narrow split-screen window a tablet shows the bar.
